title: Individual Vanadium Dopants Form Deep In-Gap States in Monolayer WS2
authors: Tianhui Zhu, Carlos A. Gonzalez, Shihao Tu, Søren Tornøe, Ivan Pelayo, Dong-Rong Wu, Zhehao Ge, Hem Prasad Bhusal, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Nobuhiko P. Kobayashi, Yuan Ping, Jairo Velasco, Aiming Yan
abstract: Point defects in atomically thin materials have a strong impact on physical properties and those that induce in-gap states are advantageous for quantum information science and engineering (QISE). However, dopant engineering consisting of well-controlled synthesis and robust identification of in-gap states is challenging. In this work, we addressed this challenge by first using finely tuned chemical vapor deposition to incorporate vanadium dopants into a monolayer WS2 (V-WS2). Next, we utilized a suite of scanned probe microscopy techniques to identify and characterize individual dopants. The latter included conductive atomic force microscopy (cAFM), low temperature scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy (STM/STS), and scanning transmission electron microscopy and unambiguously revealed that vanadium dopants form deep in-gap states 0.35 eV above the valence band maximum in V-WS2. Our experimental results are well supported by first principles calculations and taken together demonstrate that V-WS2 is a promising platform for QISE applications.
summary: This work addresses the challenge of defect engineering in 2D materials by doping monolayer $	ext{WS}_2$ with Vanadium ($	ext{V}$). Using a combination of CVD synthesis and advanced scanning probe microscopy (STM/STS, cAFM), the authors experimentally confirmed that these dopants introduce distinct deep electronic states into the band gap. This establishes $	ext{V-WS}_2$ as a promising platform for quantum information science applications.
main_problem: The challenge of engineering dopants in atomically thin materials to reliably create and identify deep electronic states suitable for quantum information science.
main_result: Vanadium dopants ($	ext{V}$) incorporated into monolayer $	ext{WS}_2$ form distinct, measurable deep in-gap electronic states ($0.35 	ext{ eV}$ above the valence band maximum).
method: The study combines synthesis via CVD with advanced characterization techniques like STM/STS and cAFM, supported by first-principles DFT calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is monolayer $	ext{WS}_2$ (a 2D TMD) doped with Vanadium ($	ext{V}$), allowing for the study of point defects and their localized electronic signatures.
key_observables: In-gap state energy levels, defect density ($	ext{cm}^{-2}$), charge transition levels ($	ext{CTLs}$), and local current maps.
important_parameters: The key energy level is $0.35 	ext{ eV}$ above the valence band maximum; defect densities are in the range of $10^{11} - 10^{12} 	ext{ cm}^{-2}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that localized electronic states observed via STM/STS correspond to specific dopant configurations ($	ext{VW}$ defects) modeled by DFT.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of characterization probes (cAFM, STM/STS, STEM), showing current maps and topography confirming defect signatures in pristine $	ext{WS}_2$ and $	ext{V-WS}_2$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the need for controlled dopant engineering; it then details the experimental characterization of defects (OS vs. V) using multiple probes, culminating in DFT confirmation of the electronic structure and suitability for QISE.
why_interesting: The ability to precisely engineer and spectroscopically confirm localized quantum states within a solid-state platform like $	ext{WS}_2$ is directly relevant to building solid-state qubits or quantum memory elements.
